title: Arignar Anna's World Tour: Lecturing on Thirukkural and Tamil Literary Heritage (1968)
summary: During his 1968 international tour across Japan, the United States, and Europe, Chief Minister C. N. Annadurai enchanted global audiences with the timeless egalitarian wisdom of Thirukkural.
full_text:
In the spring of 1968, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. N. Annadurai embarked upon an extensive international tour, delivering lectures across prestigious institutions in Japan, the United States, and Western Europe.

At the University of Tokyo and later in New York, international scholars inquired about the distinctiveness of Tamil heritage:
"Mr. Annadurai, international discourse often views Indian philosophy almost exclusively through the prism of Sanskrit scriptures. What unique contribution does classical Tamil literature offer to world thought?"

Anna responded with captivating eloquence:
"Distinguished scholars, consider our two-thousand-year-old classical masterpiece, the Thirukkural, composed by the weaver-philosopher Thiruvalluvar.

Most ancient ethical treatises are bound to specific deities, tribal rituals, or dogmatic theological systems. Yet in the thirteen hundred and thirty couplets of the Thirukkural, you will not find the name of a single sectarian god, a single religion, or a single parochial boundary!
Its foundational axiom is: 'Pirappokkum Ella Uyirkkum'—'All human beings are equal by birth!' Written centuries before the modern declarations of human rights, it addresses humanity as one indivisible family. It speaks of domestic love, civic integrity, economic industry, and compassionate statecraft. It is not the scripture of a sect; it is the universal moral code of humanity!"

International scholars were enchanted by Anna’s exposition, recognizing that classical Tamil humanism anticipated modern universal ethics by millennia.
